(Evansville, Indiana) | college = * [[Evansville Purple Aces men's basketball|Evansville]] (2016–2018) * [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri]] (2019–2021) | draftyear = 2021 | career_start = 2021 | years1 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021]]–[[2022–23 NBA G League season|2023]] | team1 = [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] | years2 = {{nbay|2022|start}} | team2 = [[Miami Heat]] | years3 = {{nbay|2022|end}} | team3 = [[Brooklyn Nets]] | years4 = [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2023]] | team4 = →[[Long Island Nets]] | years5 = {{nbay|2023|start}}–present | team5 = Miami Heat | years6 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2024]] | team6 = →Sioux Falls Skyforce | highlights = * First-team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] – Coaches (2021) * Second-team All-SEC – [[Associated Press|AP]] (2021) * SEC All-Defensive Team (2021) * [[Missouri Valley Conference|MVC]] Most Improved Team (2018) * MVC All-Freshman Team (2017) }} '''Dru Smith''' (born December 30, 1997) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Miami Heat]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Evansville Purple Aces men's basketball|Evansville Purple Aces]] and the [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri Tigers]]. ==High school career== Smith attended [[FJ Reitz High School]] in [[Evansville, Indiana]]. In his junior season he averaged 10.5 points, 5.4 rebounds and 4.5 assists per game as a starting [[point guard]] alongside Jaelan Sanford and Alex Stein. Smith helped his team achieve a 29–2 record and reach the Class 4A state title game.{{cite web |last=Napier |first=Briar |title=The "hidden jewel" of Evansville: Dru Smith thriving after leaving only home he ever knew |url=https://www.columbiamissourian.com/sports/mizzou_mens_basketball/the-hidden-jewel-of-evansville-dru-smith-thriving-after-leaving-only-home-he-ever-knew/article_c9a2d508-4ead-11ea-ad25-4fe56f820d82.html |website=[[Columbia Missourian]] |access-date=November 13, 2020 |date=February 13, 2020}} As a senior, he averaged 20.8 points, 7.3 assists, seven rebounds and 4.1 steals per game, leading Reitz to a 22–5 record and the Class 4A regional finals. Smith was named to the Indiana All-Star team.{{cite web |last=Neddenriep |first=Kyle |title=Build-A-Team: Putting together the best Evansville Reitz basketball team |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/high-school/2020/04/05/indiana-basketball-evansville-reitz-best-players-history-dru-smith-daimion-garrett/2947813001/ |website=[[The Indianapolis Star]] |access-date=November 13, 2020 |date=April 5, 2020}} He committed to playing college basketball for [[Evansville Purple Aces men's basketball|Evansville]] over offers from [[Ball State Cardinals men's basketball|Ball State]], [[Northern Kentucky Norse men's basketball|Northern Kentucky]], [[South Alabama Jaguars men's basketball|South Alabama]] and [[Indiana State Sycamores men's basketball|Indiana State]].{{cite web |last=Hickey |first=Pat |title=Former Evansville guard Dru Smith commits to Missouri basketball |url=https://www.courierpress.com/story/sports/college/evansville/2018/04/27/former-evansville-guard-dru-smith-commits-missouri-basketball/557885002/ |website=[[Evansville Courier & Press]] |access-date=November 13, 2020 |date=April 27, 2018}} Smith was drawn to the school because it was close to home.{{cite web |last=Allar |first=Daniel |title=Simmons: Reitz's Smith "a great fit" for UE |url=http://archive.courierpress.com/sports/college/evansville/simmons-reitzs-smith-a-great-fit-for-ue-244bbd3e-1458-2c2e-e053-0100007f69e1-347241342.html |website=[[Evansville Courier & Press]] |access-date=November 13, 2020 |date=November 12, 2015}} ==College career== ===Evansville=== On February 22, 2017, Smith scored a freshman season-high 19 points for Evansville, making five [[three-pointer]]s, in a 109–83 loss to [[2016–17 Wichita State Shockers men's basketball team|Wichita State]].{{cite web |title=Dru Smith Has Career Game Against Wichita State |url=https://city-countyobserver.com/dru-smith-has-career-game-against-wichita-state/ |website=City-County Observer |access-date=November 13, 2020 |date=February 22, 2017}} As a freshman, he averaged 5.3 points, 2.9 assists and 2.6 rebounds per game, earning [[Missouri Valley Conference]] (MVC) All-Freshman Team honors.{{cite web |last=Hickey |first=Pat |title=Simmons: Dru Smith has made 'huge' gains after solid freshman season for UE basketball |url=https://www.courierpress.com/story/sports/college/evansville/2017/10/04/simmons-dru-smith-has-made-huge-gains-after-solid-freshman-season-ue-basketball/733167001/ |website=[[Evansville Courier & Press]] |access-date=November 13, 2020 |date=October 4, 2017}} On December 5, 2017, Smith recorded a sophomore season-high 25 points, shooting 11-of-13 from the field, seven assists and four steals in a 91–76 win over [[2017–18 Bowling Green Falcons men's basketball team|Bowling Green]].{{cite web |title=Smith has career-high 25, Evansville beats Bowling Green |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2017/12/05/smith-has-career-high-25-evansville-beats-bowling-green/108350974/ |website=[[USA Today]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=November 13, 2020 |date=December 5, 2017}} As a sophomore, he averaged 13.7 points, 4.6 assists and two steals per game, leading the MVC with a 48.2 three-point field goal percentage.{{cite web |last=Moore |first=CJ |title=The path to a resurgent Missouri begins with Dru Smith |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1050577/2019/07/02/the-path-to-a-resurgent-missouri-begins-with-dru-smith/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=November 14, 2020 |date=July 2, 2019}} He was named to the MVC Most Improved Team. ===Missouri=== After his sophomore season, Smith transferred to [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri]] over offers from [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]] and [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech]].{{cite web |last=Schiffer |first=Alex |title=Connection to Mizzou assistant helped land Evansville transfer Dru Smith |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/sec/university-of-missouri/article210111089.html |website=[[The Kansas City Star]] |access-date=November 14, 2020 |date=April 29, 2018}} He sat out the following season due to [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] transfer rules. On November 12, 2019, he posted his first career double-double of 22 points and 10 rebounds in a 63–58 overtime loss to [[2019–20 Xavier Musketeers men's basketball team|Xavier]].{{cite news |title=No. 21 Xavier rallies past Missouri 63-58 in overtime |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401169789 |access-date=November 14, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 12, 2019}} On February 15, 2020, he scored a junior season-high 28 points in an 85–73 victory over 11th-ranked [[2019–20 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team|Auburn]].{{cite web |last=Walljasper |first=Joe |title=Dru Smith, Pinson each score 28 points as Mizzou upsets No. 11 Auburn 85-73 |url=https://www.foxsports.com/midwest/story/dru-smith-pinson-each-score-28-points-as-mizzou-upsets-no-11-auburn-85-73-021520 |website=[[Fox Sports]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=November 14, 2020 |date=February 15, 2020}} As a junior, Smith averaged 12.7 points, 4.2 rebounds, 3.9 assists and 2.1 steals per game. He recorded 64 steals, which led the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) and ranked sixth in program history.{{cite web |last=Hollins |first=Tyler |title=Dru Smith named to preseason All-SEC second team |url=https://www.lebanondemocrat.com/sports/national/dru-smith-named-to-preseason-all-sec-second-team/article_67dccad3-dbd5-5ae0-8109-28bdb7ea5a3c.html |website=[[Lebanon Democrat]] |access-date=November 14, 2020 |date=November 12, 2020 |archive-date=November 16, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201116035516/https://www.lebanondemocrat.com/sports/national/dru-smith-named-to-preseason-all-sec-second-team/article_67dccad3-dbd5-5ae0-8109-28bdb7ea5a3c.html |url-status=dead }} As a senior, Smith averaged 14.3 points, 3.8 assists, 3.5 rebounds and 2.1 steals per game.{{cite news |title=Heat's Dru Smith: Joins Heat's summer team |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/heats-dru-smith-joins-heats-summer-team/ |access-date=September 2, 2021 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=July 30, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Miami Heat / Sioux Falls Skyforce (2021–2023)=== After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Smith joined the [[Miami Heat]] for the 2021 [[NBA Summer League]]{{cite web |last=Beguiristain |first=Joe |date=August 1, 2021 |title=2021 Miami HEAT Summer League Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-announce-summer-league-roster-2021 |access-date=September 11, 2021 |website=NBA.com}}{{cite news|first=Anthony|last=Kristensen|title=Smith, Tilmon playing in NBA Summer League|url=https://www.columbiamissourian.com/sports/mizzou_mens_basketball/smith-tilmon-playing-in-nba-summer-league/article_a8d529e0-fafd-11eb-bc37-1ba26373d151.html|work=[[Columbia Missourian]]|date=August 11, 2021|access-date=September 2, 2021}} and on September 10, he signed a contract with the Heat.{{cite web |last=Moorhead |first=Couper |date=September 10, 2021 |title=HEAT SIGNS POTTER, SMART AND SMITH |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-signs-potter-smart-smith |access-date=September 11, 2021 |website=NBA.com}} He was waived prior to the start of the season and joined the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] as an affiliate player.{{cite news |last=Engelhardt |first=Gordon |title=Reitz graduate Dru Smith waived by Miami Heat, appears headed to NBA G League |url=https://www.courierpress.com/story/sports/2021/10/19/reitz-grad-dru-smith-waived-miami-heat-expected-join-g-league/8516178002/ |access-date=October 27, 2021 |work=[[Evansville Courier & Press]] |date=October 19, 2021}} On February 1, 2022, Smith was waived after being ruled out for the season with a knee injury.{{cite web |title=SKYFORCE ACQUIRES CHANDLER HUTCHISON |url=https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-acquires-chandler-hutchison/ |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 1, 2022 |date=February 1, 2022}} On October 13, 2022, Smith was signed to a two-way contract with the Miami Heat.{{cite web |title=HEAT CONVERT DRU SMITH TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-convert-dru-smith-to-two-way-contract |website=NBA.com |date=October 13, 2022|access-date=October 14, 2022}} He was waived by the Heat on November 13, and subsequently re-joined the Skyforce.{{cite web |title=Heat Sign Orlando Robinson to Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-sign-orlando-robinson-to-two-way-contract |website=NBA |access-date=November 14, 2022 |date=November 13, 2022}} On November 25, 2022, Smith was re-signed to a two-way contract with the Heat{{cite web |title=HEAT SIGN DRU SMITH TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-sign-dru-smith-to-two-way-contract |website=NBA.com |date=November 25, 2022|access-date=November 25, 2022}} and subsequently waived on December 11, and re-joined the Skyforce two days later.{{cite tweet|number=1601987170935480320|user=MiamiHEAT|title=OFFICIAL: The Miami HEAT have signed Orlando Robinson to a two-way contract and have waived Dru Smith.|author=Miami HEAT|date=December 11, 2022|access-date=December 11, 2022}} ===Brooklyn Nets (2023)=== On January 13, 2023, Smith signed a two-way contract with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web |title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Dru Smith |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-sign-dru-smith |website=NBA.com |access-date=January 14, 2023 |date=January 13, 2023}} In 10 appearances for Brooklyn, Smith averaged 3.3 points, 1.5 rebounds and 1.7 assists. ===Second stint with Heat (2023–present)=== On July 1, 2023, Smith signed a two-way contract with the [[Miami Heat]]{{cite web|title=HEAT SIGN DRU SMITH TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-sign-dru-smith-to-two-way-contract-2|website=NBA.com|date=July 1, 2023|access-date=July 1, 2023}} and on October 21, his deal was converted into a standard contract.{{cite web|title=HEAT SIGN DRU SMITH TO STANDARD CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-sign-dru-smith-to-standard-contract|website=NBA.com|date=October 21, 2023|access-date=October 21, 2023}} On November 24, 2023, it was announced that Smith would miss the remainder of the [[2023–24 NBA season]] due to an [[ACL injury]] sustained during a game against the [[2023–24 Cleveland Cavaliers season|Cleveland Cavaliers]] on November 22. The head coach of the Heat, [[Erik Spoelstra]], blamed the court design at [[Rocket Mortgage FieldHouse]] for the incident.{{cite magazine|first=Shandel|last=Richardson|title=Miami Heat's Dru Smith Out For Season Due To Knee Injury|url=https://www.si.com/nba/heat/miami-news/miami-heats-dru-smith-out-for-season-due-to-knee-injury|magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=November 24, 2023|access-date=November 29, 2023}} On March 6, 2024, he was waived by the Heat.{{cite web|title=HEAT SIGN PATTY MILLS|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-sign-patty-mills|website=NBA.com|date=March 6, 2024|access-date=March 7, 2024}} On July 1, 2024, Smith signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Heat.{{cite web|title=HEAT SIGN DRU SMITH TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-sign-dru-smith-to-two-way-contract-3|website=NBA.com|date=July 1, 2024|access-date=July 1, 2024}} He played in 15 games for Miami, averaging 6.3 points, 2.6 rebounds and 1.6 assists. On December 24, it was announced that Smith had suffered a season-ending [[torn Achilles tendon]].{{Cite web|title=Sources: Heat's Dru Smith has torn Achilles, done for season|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/43142951|access-date=December 25, 2024|website=ESPN.com|date=December 24, 2024 |language=en|last=Charania|first=Shams|author-link=Shams Charania}} On August 16, 2025, Smith re-signed with the Heat on a three-year, $7.9 million contract.{{Cite web |date=August 16, 2025 |title=Heat Re-Sign Dru Smith |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-re-sign-dru-smith |access-date=October 27, 2025 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== {{NBA player
